VBO:0200293.summary: Alert and sometimes reserved with strangers in JCF’s standard, the Carlin Pinscher is a developing North American companion type. Its ancestry is chiefly Pug and Miniature Pinscher, with other breeds used during development. JCF describes dogs that join walks and quiet time at home; the program’s own account allows variation, rather than a fixed miniature-Rottweiler identity.
VBO:0200293.shortDescription: An alert North American companion type, chiefly from Pug and Miniature Pinscher ancestry, with some reserve toward strangers.

sources.title: JCF Carlin Pinschers — original breed standard
sources.evidence: Entire actual own standard reread. North American companion development, alert well-balanced often reserved toward strangers. Literal natural tail permitted equally with docked; at rest level with topline/excited erect, no length or precise terminal shape specified. Own square/wedge head, moderate projected muzzle, almond eyes, natural triangular button ears, functional balanced sturdy body/legs, short glossy coat and tanpoints. No parental average. Correction review 2026-10-06: Independently reread substantive standard and FAQ 2026-10-06. Standard states alert/balanced/often standoffish with strangers; NorthAmerican companion development primarily Pug/MinPin with other contributors. FAQ explicitly rejects miniature-Rottweiler and fixed purebred framing and records walks/couch routines. Medical, family safety and inherited guarantees omitted.
